0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Stanckrd ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 February 1981, after the draft finalized by the Umbrellas Secrional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Iustrurnents Division Council.

0.2 This standard
suggestions were

revised

was first published in the year i964. Since then many received for its improvement. This standard is being to take care of the suggestions received from time to time.

0.3 Umbrellas are being manufactured in the country in iarge quantity both for large domestic consumpticm and export. By and large, the manufacturers of umbrellas procure the different parts from different component manufacturers. It is, therefore, necessary that Indian Standards should be made available for the complete umbrella as we!l as for the components. 0.4 The sizes of umbrelIas are usuaily known by the length of the main The usual lengths are 686, 635, 584, 533, ribs expressed in millimetre. 483, 432 and 381 mm and the umbrellas are accordingly designated. 0.5 This standard deals with umbrella which are necessary for the assembiy of that the dimensions of the notch end of observed as any undue protuberance will and will tear it in a short time. 0.6 the his are ribs and lays down dimensions I t is recommended umbrellas. the main rib should be strictly foul against the umbrella eioth

This standard contains clauses which will call for agreement bet ween purchaser and the supplier and which permit the purchaser to use option for selection to suit his requirements. The relevant clauses 9 and 10.

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. `Rules for rounding of rmmeric~l wducs ( rw~$~d).
